name: Dutch Windmill
description: First introduced from Germany. At first it was only used for grinding powder and the like. By the 16th and 17th centuries, windmills were of particularly great significance to the Dutch economy. At that time, the Netherlands held a leading position in the world's commerce. Various raw materials were transported from various waterways to windmills for processing, including: wood from Nordic countries and countries along the Baltic Sea, hemp seeds and linseeds from Germany, and cinnamon and pepper from India and Southeast Asia. In the suburbs of Rotterdam and Amsterdam, the great ports of the Netherlands, there are many windmills, sawmills and paper mills. As the Dutch people carried out large-scale land reclamation projects from the sea, windmills played a huge role in this arduous project. The first step was to equip the windmill with a movable canopy, and then they mounted the windmill's canopy on rollers. This kind of windmill is called a Dutch windmill.
